Status language

Verified shipped, tested and audited. Blocked waiting on an external dependency. Deferred intentionally not built.

A phase is only marked verified after the full suite passes and three independent reviews agree.

How to read the evidence
  • Scope is frozen at 08de0e8; documentation commits are excluded.
  • Every screenshot is a live build capture, not a mockup.
  • Audit session IDs are recorded verbatim in section 16.
  • Push delivery (A5) is described as blocked, never as shipped.

The interface is no longer a set of screens. It is one event system with a shared privacy contract.

This document records what was built, what was measured, and what remains outside the release.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordExecutive summary
Release position

The app now reacts to the moment.

Live events, chat management and presence share one privacy-aware system.

Fifty-four commits replaced polling and silent state changes with a typed notification backbone, contextual banners, honest preference controls, everyday chat tools, and a server-enforced privacy model for online status, typing and read receipts. The work was delivered in four tracks and closed with 155 passing tests.

One event model

Notifications are typed, deduplicated and routable.

A single service now feeds Activity, in-app banners, local system alerts, the launcher badge and cold-start routing. Unknown payloads fail closed instead of leaking technical text.

Quiet by default

Users choose what reaches them, and when.

Master switch, per-category gates, preview privacy, quiet hours, sound and vibration are all observable and persisted. Presence, typing and receipts are separate, server-backed permissions.

Everyday chat

The small actions now exist.

Mute windows, manual unread, drafts, unread divider, scroll-to-bottom count, search, copy, retry and clear-read turn the chat list into a usable inbox.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordArchitecture
Architecture

One event path from Postgres to the screen.

Services own state.
Widgets only render it.

The notification and chat systems were deliberately split: durable events arrive through Supabase, ephemeral signals travel over the chat channel, and every surface consumes the same typed state rather than subscribing independently.

Durable
notificationsRealtime publication, SELECT scoped by notif_read.
→
Service
NotificationServiceDedupe, unread count, mark read, lifecycle, reconnect.
→
Policy
NotificationPresenterCategory, preview, quiet-hours and route gates.
→
Surface
Banner · Activity
Local · BadgeOne event, four renderers, one source.
In-app bannerQueued, 4s default, swipe/close, live-region semantics.
ActivityTyped list, filters, day groups, swipe-to-read.
System alertFour Android channel combinations by category.
Launcher badgeActivity plus chat unread, preference-gated.
Ephemeral chat channel

Presence, typing and read signals travel on chat:<connectionId>. The client tracks only when the peer allows presence, broadcasts typing with a 2s throttle, and treats read events as hints until the server timestamp is reloaded.

No database writes for typing. No client-clock authority for Seen.
Failure posture

Realtime joins refresh an expired session first, then retry with backoff. Privacy state that has not loaded disables the related controls. Unsupported platforms no-op instead of throwing, and sign-out resets every service.

Service inventory

NotificationService

Typed notification state, realtime channel, dedupe, unread list/count, mark read, lifecycle, sign-out reset.

NotificationPresenter

Chooses banner kind, applies category/quiet/preview/privacy gates, plays match/message feedback, suppresses the active screen.

LocalNotificationService

System notifications, Android channels (four sound/vibration combinations per category), permission state/request, tap and cold-start routing.

AppBadgeService

Launcher badge from activity + chat unread, preference gate, serialized writes, web no-op, sign-out reset.

ConnectivityService

Online state, offline strip source, reconnect refresh for notifications and conversations.

DraftService

Per-conversation drafts, debounce, restore, clear on send/sign-out.

ChatPrivacyService

Server-backed presence/typing/receipt switches, coalesced load, optimistic save with revert, reset on sign-out.

Haptics

Named intents, throttle, platform and preference gates, match pattern.

SoundService

Shared player over messages/newmatch/splash assets, preference/lifecycle gates, debounce, serialized init.

AppShellState

Selected tab, Activity/Requests open flags for route-aware suppression.

AppRouter / navigatorKey

Queue-safe routing from services and cold starts.

Rule: no widget talks to Supabase for notification or presence state. Widgets observe a service; the service owns retries, gating and teardown.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack A / A0
Track A / A0

A typed event backbone.

One source of truth for Activity, banners, local alerts and badges.

Before A0, unread state was assembled ad hoc and every surface interpreted notification payloads differently. The foundation introduced a typed model, a single realtime service and a router that can act before or after the first frame.

What shipped
  • AppNotification with known kinds, defensive parsing, payload fallbacks, read state and copy/row adapters.
  • NotificationService owns the realtime channel, dedupe by id, unread count, mark-one/all, lifecycle refresh, sign-out reset and reconnect.
  • AppRouter and a global navigator key let banners, Activity, local alerts and cold starts route to Activity, Requests, Chat or Profile.
  • ActivityService replaced and every caller migrated.
  • Server: notifications added to the realtime publication with SELECT scoped by the existing read policy; list RPC enriched with actor, skill, role and connection status.
AppNotification contract
Kinds
request · accepted · declined · feedback · moderation · unknown
Parsing
defensive, unknown-safe
Fallbacks
payload → row columns
State
read / unread, copyWith
Adapters
toRow for tests and seeds

An unknown kind renders as a neutral Activity row. It never throws and never prints raw SQL or payload text.

Event routing
KindDefault destinationContext carried
requestRequests · incomingconnection_id, actor
acceptedChat roomconnection_id, peer, role
declinedRequests · incomingconnection_id
feedbackActivitynotification_id
moderationActivitynotification_id

Why it mattered: A1, A3, A4, B2 and C3 all attach to this one model. Without it, each surface would have grown its own parser and its own definition of unread.

Realtime lifecycle

Join

Refresh an expired session, open the channel, then mark joined only after the subscription acknowledges.

Recover

Back off on JWT or channel errors, resubscribe, and refresh the unread list on success.

Reset

Sign-out clears unread state, cancels the channel and resets the router so the next account starts clean.

Migration contract
IDGuaranteeFailure mode
001Realtime insert visible only to the owning userRow stays in Activity after refresh
002Activity carries actor, skill, role and statusNeutral row, no technical text

Contract: the payload remains the source of ids; joins only decorate. A missing actor or skill degrades the row, never the unread count.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack A / A1
Track A / A1

Live events, without leaving the screen.

One banner at a time.
Route-aware, never over the active chat.

A1 made live activity visible in context. The old bottom match sheet was replaced by a top banner system that queues, coalesces and suppresses itself on screens where it would interrupt the task.

Standard banner

Request, decline, feedback.

Four-second default, close or swipe to dismiss, tap to route, live-region semantics and reduced-motion support. Grouped per conversation so a burst never becomes a stack.

Match banner

“You're now Pals with X.”

Skill line and Say hello action, about seven seconds, once per connection, persisted across restarts. It pre-empts a standard banner and restores the queue afterwards.

Message banner

Sender, preview, tap to chat.

Emitted only for messages outside the active room and not authored by the current user. Same-conversation messages coalesce instead of stacking.

Suppression matrix
Current surfaceBehaviourWhy
ActivityNotification banners suppressedThe list is already visible.
Requests (pushed)Request banners suppressedAvoid duplicate decisions.
Active chat roomThat conversation's banners suppressedMessages are on screen.
Any other surfaceBanner shown and queuedKeep the user in context.
Realtime hardening
  • Expired session refreshed before join
  • Backoff on JWT/channel errors
  • Joined state tracked explicitly
  • Recovery on token refresh and resume
Accessibility

Banners use a polite live region, expose one primary action, keep 44px targets, and switch to a static presentation when animations are disabled. 360px and 200% text are covered by widget tests.

Timing and queue
BannerDwellQueue rule
Standard4sOne visible; next waits
Match~7sPre-empts; previous restored
Message4sCoalesces per conversation
Nudge10sQueued behind the active banner
Reduced motion

When animations are disabled, the banner appears without translation and the match moment uses the static presentation. Grouping still applies, so a burst of messages produces one update rather than a strobe.

Match persistence

A match banner is shown once per connection and remembered across restarts, so reopening the app cannot replay the celebration.

Message coalescing

Several messages from one conversation update the visible banner instead of queuing one per message; different conversations still queue.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack A / A2 · A6
Track A / A2 · A6

Feedback feels intentional, never technical.

Physical cues and one snackbar contract.
Preferences always win.

Two phases closed the feedback layer. A2 replaced raw haptics with named intents and added gated sound; A6 replaced ad-hoc snackbars and raw error strings with a single feedback helper and a friendly-error allowlist.

A2 · Haptics and sound

Named cues, throttled and gated.

  • Intents: selection, tap, toggle, impact, success, warning, error, match.
  • 50ms per-intent throttle; web/desktop no-op; vibration preference gate.
  • SoundService reuses messages.wav, newmatch.wav and splash.wav.
  • 150ms debounce, serialized init, stop on route change, lifecycle gate.
  • Enabling sound or vibration in Settings previews the choice.
A6 · AppFeedback

One snackbar contract.

  • Info, success and error tones with icon and duration (4s / 3s / 6s).
  • One action, clearSnackBars, and a dialog-scoped variant.
  • Adopted across home, chat, matches, requests, block list, explore, account and settings.
  • Undo snackbars use an explicit five-second duration.
  • Technical leakage rejected before the friendly allowlist.
Cue matrix
EventHapticSoundGate
New matchmatch patternnewmatch.wavcategory + quiet hours
Incoming messageimpactmessages.wavpreview / quiet hours
Request sent or acceptedsuccess—vibration preference
Decline or undowarning—single cue only
Destructive confirmationerror—vibration preference
Toggle, chip, tabselection / tap—50ms throttle

Leak guard: Postgrest text, SQLSTATE codes, varying() errors and auth internals are rejected before the allowlist. Validation copy — including password digit rules and account-deletion messages — is preserved verbatim.

Sound assets
AssetUsed for
newmatch.wavMatch moment only
messages.wavIncoming message while outside the room
splash.wavStartup, once

Single cue

Raw haptics were removed from request cards, so a preference cannot be bypassed and decline does not double-cue.

Preview

Enabling sound or vibration in Settings plays the cue once, confirming the choice without a test screen.

One path: every cue goes through the same preference check. There is no raw platform call left in a widget that could bypass a disabled sound or vibration setting.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack A / A3
Track A / A3

Notification preferences that tell the truth.

Every switch maps to a real gate.
No fictional OS copy.

A3 turned a thin preference store into an observable model and gave it a dedicated settings page. Each category, preview, quiet-hours window, sound and vibration choice is applied by the presenter before anything reaches a surface.

What shipped
  • Master switch plus messages, requests/matches, activity, previews, quiet hours, sound and vibration.
  • Presenter gates each event kind; quiet hours suppress sound and haptics while banners still appear.
  • Preview privacy replaces message text with “New message” when previews are off.
  • Settings page with delivery state, permission status, categories, preview example, adaptive time pickers and Pals-only context.
  • Master off disables categories without erasing their saved values; the Settings root summary stays accurate.

Honesty fix: fictional OS-permission copy was removed. The page reports the actual permission state and never promises delivery it cannot provide.

ControlEffectWhen master off
MessagesMessage banners and local alertsGated off, value retained
Requests / matchesRequest, decline and match eventsGated off, value retained
ActivityFeedback and moderation rowsGated off, value retained
PreviewMessage body versus “New message”Preview hidden
Quiet hoursNo sound or haptics; banners remainNo effect

Quiet-hours behaviour

The window is evaluated per event on the device. It suppresses audio and haptics only; it does not mark anything read or hide the banner.

Preview privacy

With previews off, the banner and system alert both read “New message”. The sender remains so the user can decide whether to open the chat.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack A / A4
Track A / A4

System notifications while the process is alive.

Permissions, channels and tap routing.
No claim beyond that.

A4 added local system notifications with real Android channels and a permission model that distinguishes “not asked” from “denied”. Taps and cold-start payloads route into the correct surface with peer context.

Platform contract
PlatformBehaviour
AndroidFour channel combinations per category (sound × vibration). POST_NOTIFICATIONS and VIBRATE declared; status icon present.
iOSUNUserNotificationCenter delegate set in AppDelegate; deployment target raised to 13.0. Compiled on macOS still required.
WebInitialization and permission APIs wired; unsupported browsers fail closed and skip silently.
Permission state

Not asked vs denied vs granted. Request from Settings; denied opens system settings; state refreshes on resume.

Tap routing

Chat, Requests, Activity or Profile, including cold start, with the peer and connection context carried in the payload.

Foreground

In-app banner is the primary cue; a duplicate system alert is suppressed while the app is visible.

Background process

Local alerts fire while the process is alive. Cancelled on logout and gated by category, quiet hours and previews.

Killed app

Not covered. That requires A5 push credentials and is explicitly outside this release claim.

Release wording: notifications work in-app and through a background process on Android. Push for killed apps is prepared but not delivered.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack B / B0
Track B / B0

The app survives a bad connection.

Refresh keeps content.
Offline is visible, not modal.

B0 added the primitives that every later quality-of-life feature depends on: pull-to-refresh that preserves state, a persistent offline strip, a correct launcher badge, and per-conversation drafts.

01

Pull to refresh

Chats, Activity, Requests (incoming and sent) and Browse. On failure the list stays and a snackbar explains the problem.

02

Offline strip

Persistent, laid out above app content rather than over the app bar. Reconnect refreshes notifications and conversations.

03

Launcher badge

Activity unread plus chat unread, master-preference gated, serialized writes, reset on sign-out, skipped on web.

04

Drafts

Per conversation, 350ms debounce, restored on open, cleared on send or sign-out, previewed as “Draft:” in the list.

Draft lifecycle
MomentBehaviourGuarantee
TypingDebounced write after 350ms of inactivityNo write per keystroke
Leaving chatDraft persists and appears in the list previewSurvives navigation
ReopeningComposer restores the draft at the cursor endNo lost text
SendingDraft cleared only after the send is acceptedNo empty composer on failure
Sign-outAll drafts clearedNo cross-account leakage
Offline behaviour

The strip occupies layout space, so it cannot cover the app bar or intercept taps. Reconnect triggers a notification refresh and a conversation reload instead of waiting for the next manual pull.

Badge arithmetic

activity unread + chat unread, capped by the platform, written serially, and reset on sign-out. Web and unsupported launchers are a no-op rather than a crash.

Connectivity transitions
TransitionBehaviour
Online → offlineStrip appears above content; current list stays
Offline → onlineNotifications and conversations refresh
Refresh failureContent retained; snackbar explains
Cold start offlineCached shell renders; actions report
No silent loss

A failed refresh never blanks a populated list, and a failed send keeps the draft and the pending row. The user sees the failure and can retry; nothing is quietly discarded.

Draft edge cases
CaseBehaviour
Send failsDraft is retained alongside the pending message
Account switchDrafts are cleared before the next account loads
Conversation deletedDraft is dropped with the thread

Refresh rule: keep what is on screen, fetch in place, and report failure. A spinner that replaces content is treated as a regression.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack B / B1
Track B / B1

Chat does the small things.

Mute, unread, drafts, divider, search, copy, retry.

B1 turned the chat room from a message list into a manageable inbox. Every action is server-persisted where it must survive a reinstall, and purely local where it does not.

Mute

Quiet one conversation.

1h, 8h, 1d, 1w or always. Muted chats suppress banners and local alerts but still count unread; the list keeps a mute icon.

Mark unread

Return to it later.

Server flag, red dot in the list, cleared when the room opens. It does not fabricate a push notification.

Scroll FAB

New messages below.

Appears with a count while scrolled up. Auto-scroll only happens when the user is already at the bottom.

Copy

Long-press, one confirmation.

Clipboard write plus a single snackbar. No duplicate system toast.

Search

Find inside the loaded room.

Results with highlight and jump. Scope is the loaded message window, stated in the sheet.

Unread divider

A visible boundary.

First unread message gets a divider, so returning to a long thread has an obvious anchor.

Mute windows
DurationStored asExpiry
1 hourmuted_until = now + 1hRe-evaluated on read
8 hoursmuted_until = now + 8hList icon disappears
1 daymuted_until = now + 1dBanners resume
1 weekmuted_until = now + 7dBanners resume
Alwaysmuted_until = nullUntil unmuted
Retry

Failed pending messages retry sequentially and stop at the first renewed failure, so a dead connection does not spin. Reconnect triggers the same path automatically.

Draft integration keeps the composer and the list preview in sync throughout.

Action persistence
ActionStored whereSurvives reinstallCleared when
Muteconnection_preferencesYesExpiry or unmute
Manual unreadconnection_preferencesYesRoom opens
DraftLocal per conversationNoSend or sign-out
Unread dividerDerived from read stateYesNext read

Search scope

Search runs over the loaded message window and says so. It does not imply full-history search that the client cannot guarantee.

Copy behaviour

Long-press writes to the clipboard and raises one snackbar. There is no second system toast and no silent failure.

Persistence: mute and manual unread survive a reinstall because they are server rows. Drafts stay on the device and are cleared on sign-out; they are deliberately not synced across devices.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack B / B2
Track B / B2

Lists and Activity carry the same rules.

One long-press vocabulary.
One clear-read contract.

B2 pushed chat management and Activity triage to the list level. Actions that were buried in the room became available from the row, and clearing read notifications became a server-side, caller-scoped operation.

Chat long-press

View profile · Mute · Mark unread · Report · Block.

The profile dialog keeps its own block and report paths. Mute and unread reuse the same services as the room, so the list and the thread never disagree.

Activity filters

All · Unread · Requests · Updates.

Counts on each filter, day groups (Today, Yesterday, date), a filtered empty state, and clear-search recovery. Realtime inserts land in the right group.

Clear-read semantics
Row stateWhat Clear read doesServer guarantee
ReadDeleted for the callerread_at is not null
UnreadKept, still countedNever touched
Other user's rowsInvisibleuser_id = auth.uid()
FailureList unchanged, error surfacedNo false success
Swipe to read

An unread row can be marked read by swipe. The row updates immediately and reconciles with the server; a failure restores the unread state and reports it.

Saved filters

Chat role/status and request incoming/sent filters persist per screen, restore on open, and reset through an explicit clear action. A filter can never strand a tab in an empty state with no way back.

Failure honesty: clear, mute and mark-unread report errors instead of pretending success. The previous optimistic-only paths were replaced with a result the surface can render.

Reset

Clear filters restores the default view and the saved filter is removed, not just visually bypassed.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack B / B3
Track B / B3

The next step, without the nag.

One prompt at a time.
Every empty state has an action.

B3 handled the moments after a request, after onboarding, and after a filter returns nothing. The rule was consistent: surface one useful next step, never block the committed action, and never stack two completion prompts.

Continue setup

Only when setup is incomplete.

Appears when onboarding was skipped or a draft exists. Resume restores the review step; dismiss persists per user and the card returns if setup is skipped again.

Profile nudge

After the request is committed.

Uses the app banner: non-blocking, SafeArea, queued, closable, ten seconds, at most once per session. It never interrupts the send.

Empty states

One clear action each.

Start swiping, view sent requests or refresh, view requests or show all, update skills or refresh categories. No dead-end copy.

Trigger matrix
SurfaceConditionAction
HomeSetup incomplete, skipped or draft existsResume review · dismiss per user
After requestSend succeeded, profile incompleteProfile nudge, once per session
Chats filtered emptyFilter returns no rowsClear filters or start a chat
Requests sent emptyNo outgoing requestsView incoming or refresh
Explore emptyNo categories for the roleUpdate skills or refresh categories

One-prompt rule: Profile shows only one completion prompt at a time. Requests never leaves the tab trapped in the sent view; back always returns to a meaningful screen.

Dismissal scope
PromptStored perReturns when
Continue setupUserSetup skipped again
Profile nudgeSessionNext session, once
What's newVersionNew version

Resume path

Resume restores the review step with its saved draft; it does not restart onboarding.

Nudge timing

The request is already committed before the nudge appears, so dismissing it never cancels the send.

Dismissal is not failure

Dismissing the resume card hides the prompt, not the draft. The setup data stays until the user completes or clears it.

One prompt at a time

Profile calculates which completion prompt to show and renders one; two prompts never compete for the same space.

Dead-end rule: every empty state names the next action and the action is reachable without leaving the current tab.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack C / C0
Track C / C0

Privacy is a contract, not a toggle.

Define the data before showing it.
Mask at the server, not the widget.

C0 added the status fields and then closed the paths that would have leaked them. The client cannot read connection read timestamps directly, and every presence or receipt value is masked to accepted Pals with the relevant permission on.

Contracts added
ContractPurposeAccess
last_seen_atPresence timestamp on the profileself only, via RPC
presence_enabledPeer may see online / last activeself write, masked read
typing_enabledPeer may see typingself write, masked read
read_receipts_enabledPeer may see Seenself write, masked read
touch_last_seenSelf-only heartbeatSECURITY DEFINER
get_pals_presenceAccepted Pals only; mask when offauthenticated
set/get_chat_privacyThree switches, server-backedauthenticated
Client may read
  • Own privacy settings
  • Peer status for accepted Pals when enabled
  • Peer read timestamp when receipts are on
  • Conversation metadata without receipt columns
Client may not read
  • Connection table read timestamps directly
  • Status for non-Pals or declined connections
  • Last seen when presence is off
  • Receipts when the peer has them off

Closing the bypass: migration 007 revokes table SELECT on connections and grants only id, participants, status, timestamps and skill columns. Read timestamps are reachable only through RPCs that apply the permission.

Masking matrix
ViewerPresence offTyping offReceipts offNot a Pal
Accepted PalNo statusNo indicatorNo Seen—
Pending requestNo statusNo indicatorNo SeenBlocked
DeclinedNo statusNo indicatorNo SeenBlocked
SelfOwn valueOwn valueOwn value—

Load failure

Switches are disabled until server state loads. A failed load shows Retry and never assumes the permissive default.

Reset

Sign-out resets the privacy service. The next account cannot inherit a previous session's switches.

Why the server owns this

A client-side hide is a suggestion. The masking lives in the RPC and the grant, so a modified client still cannot read a status the peer turned off.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack C / C1 · C2
Track C / C1 · C2

Online, typing, and nothing more.

Presence is a heartbeat.
Typing is a broadcast, never a write.

Presence and typing were built on the existing chat channel. Both are gated by the peer's privacy flags, both tear down cleanly on leave, and neither exposes a status to someone who is not an accepted Pal.

C1 · Presence

A 60-second foreground heartbeat.

  • Heartbeat and conversation refresh while resumed.
  • Disabled when privacy has not loaded or presence is off.
  • Chat list shows green Online or muted Active Nm/h/d; message time stays visible.
  • Room subscribes to chat:<connectionId>, filters the peer by exact user id.
  • Channels removed on leave, privacy-off or error without re-entrant teardown.
C2 · Typing

Three dots, two seconds, zero rows.

  • Broadcast on the existing chat channel with a 2s throttle.
  • Peer expiry after 3s; stop on empty, send or leave.
  • No database writes.
  • Gated by the local typing setting and the peer's typing flag.
  • Works with presence off: the channel joins without tracking presence.
  • Typing appears before the first message; the pre-first-message match card stays.
Lifecycle
01
ResumeSession refreshed; privacy state loaded before any track.
02
HeartbeatSelf last-seen advanced every 60s while presence is on.
03
TrackRoom joins the channel and tracks only when allowed.
04
SignalTyping and read broadcasts are throttled and peer-scoped.
05
TeardownLeave, pause, privacy-off and error all remove the channel.
Masking rules

When presence is off, the peer receives no online state and no last-seen value. When typing is off, the indicator never renders. When receipts are off, read timestamps are null even if the rows exist.

Edge cases covered

Re-enabling presence retracks; typing-only mode still joins; a failed channel recovers; a typing event can arrive before the first message without breaking the match card.

Signal rules
SignalTransportCadenceExpiry / teardown
PresenceChannel track60s heartbeatLeave, pause, privacy off
TypingBroadcast2s throttle3s peer expiry
ReceiptBroadcast + reloadTrailing flush60s refresh
Online labelServer contractOn list refreshMasked when off

No status leak

A peer who is not an accepted Pal never receives a track, a typing event or a read timestamp, regardless of the local toggle.

No stale state

The 60s heartbeat and the conversation refresh mean a closed app becomes “Active Nm” rather than staying online forever.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordTrack C / C3
Track C / C3

Seen means the server says so.

One label, under the last own message.
No device-clock authority.

C3 added read receipts without reopening the bypass C0 closed. A throttled broadcast is only a hint; the displayed time is always reloaded from the server, so a skewed device clock cannot produce a false Seen.

Receipt path
01

Peer reads

Mark-read commits on the server.

02

Broadcast hint

A throttled read event with a trailing flush reaches the room.

03

Server reload

The client reloads the conversation timestamp; the broadcast value is discarded.

04

Render

Seen appears only under the last own message, when receipts are enabled and the timestamp covers it.

Gating
ConditionResult
Peer receipts offNo Seen, even if the read row exists
Older own messageNo label; only the last own message qualifies
Peer has not read that farNo label
App backgroundedRead broadcasts paused; 60s refresh reconciles

Transport note: receipts use a broadcast plus a 60-second conversation refresh instead of publishing connections, because C0 made read timestamps RPC-only. A read event can arrive before mark-read commits; the server refresh is the source of truth.

Data contracts

Seven migrations make the interface true.

All applied live.
All committed.

The UI is only trustworthy because the database owns the hard rules: who may see a status, which read timestamp is exposed, what a mute stores, and whether a clear-read operation can touch another user's rows.

IDMigrationPurposeContract

Adds public.notifications to supabase_realtime (guarded) and grants SELECT to authenticated; row visibility stays scoped by notif_read (user_id = auth.uid()).		notifications → realtime

Recreates list_notifications with actor name/avatar, skill, role, and connection status joins while keeping payload as the source of ids.		list_notifications

Adds connection_preferences (user_id, connection_id, muted_until, marked_unread), SELECT-only RLS, set_connection_mute, set_connection_unread, get_connection_preferences, and appends muted/marked fields to get_conversations.		connection_preferences

Adds clear_read_notifications(), a SECURITY DEFINER delete limited to user_id = auth.uid() and read_at is not null.		clear_read_notifications

Adds last_seen_at and three privacy flags to profiles; adds touch_last_seen, set/get_chat_privacy, get_pals_presence; appends peer presence/typing/receipts/read fields to get_conversations. Realtime topic ACL cannot be installed from the management role (see limitations).		chat_privacy RPCs

7/7
applied live
0
invalid live paths
3
privacy migrations

Known boundary: the management role cannot alter realtime.messages, which is owned by supabase_realtime_admin. Chat topics rely on unguessable connection UUIDs and client-side privacy gating; a dashboard-authored realtime ACL would be required for server-side topic authorization.

Read-only by design

Notification reads are scoped by the existing notif_read policy. Connection read timestamps are not in the table grant at all; they are reachable only through the RPCs that apply the receipt toggle.

Write path

Mute, manual unread, privacy switches and clear-read are all RPCs. The client does not construct arbitrary updates against these tables.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordLimitations
Limitations

What is explicitly not claimed.

Documented, owned, outside the shipped scope.

The release has one external blocker and five accepted boundaries. None is an unresolved defect inside the sixteen verified phases, but each changes what the product may safely promise.

ItemStatus and handling
A5 pushBlocked on Firebase project/config, APNs key, web VAPID, and a service account. Killed-app alerts and guaranteed iOS background delivery are unavailable. In-app, Activity, badges, foreground banners, local notifications while alive, and server reconciliation remain.
Realtime topic ACLThe management role cannot alter realtime.messages (owned by supabase_realtime_admin). chat:<connectionId> topics rely on unguessable UUIDs and client-side privacy gating. Add a dashboard-authored policy if server-side ACLs are required.
Read-receipt transportC3 uses a read broadcast + 60s conversation refresh instead of publishing connections, because C0 made connection read timestamps RPC-only to honor the receipt toggle.
iOS buildSource/config verified but not compiled on this Windows host. A macOS build and device pass are still required.
D-02 review promptDeferred until a store listing exists.
Background receiptsA read event can arrive before mark_messages_read commits; server refresh reconciles within the next poll.

Release hold: none inside the shipped scope.

A5 is a delivery gap, not a hidden failure. The correct public claim is in-app notifications, Activity, badges and local alerts while the process is alive — not killed-app push.

Operational follow-ups
  • Add Firebase, APNs, VAPID and a service account to unblock A5.
  • Compile and device-test iOS on macOS.
  • Add a dashboard realtime topic policy if server-side ACLs are required.
Product follow-ups
  • D-02 waits for a real store listing.
  • Background receipts reconcile within the next poll.
  • Consider a broader read for presence if product wants roots, not leaves.
Safe release wording
ClaimStateUse instead
Killed-app pushNot shipped“Notifications work in-app and while the Android process is alive.”
Guaranteed iOS backgroundNot shipped“Local alerts are wired; device delivery still needs a macOS build.”
Server-side realtime ACLPartial“Topics use unguessable connection ids and client privacy gating.”
Store review promptDeferred“Planned once a published store listing exists.”

A5 unblock checklist

Firebase project · Android/iOS/web apps · APNs .p8 · VAPID key · service account. No client redesign is required.

Device QA

A macOS build and a physical VoiceOver/TalkBack pass remain recommended before public release.

What is not on this list: crashes, data loss, unrecoverable states or silent write failures inside the shipped surfaces. The limitations are scope boundaries and external dependencies, not hidden defects.

Operations

What the credentials unlock.

A5 is an infrastructure task, not a redesign.

Nothing in the client needs to be re-architected for push. The remaining work is identity: a Firebase project, platform configuration files, an APNs key, a web VAPID key and a service account for the sender.

Required inputs
CredentialPurpose
Firebase projectAndroid, iOS, web apps registered to the release application id.
android/app/google-services.jsonAndroid Firebase identity.
ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plistiOS Firebase identity.
APNs .p8 + Key ID + Team IDApple push authorization.
Web VAPID public keyBrowser push subscription identity.
Firebase service account JSONEdge function authentication to FCM HTTP v1.
Safe state today
  • In-app banners route correctly
  • Activity receives realtime inserts
  • Local alerts work while alive
  • Badges reflect unread totals
  • Resume reconciles missed events
  • No killed-app claim is made
When credentials arrive
01

Register the apps

Create the Firebase project and register the release application id for Android, iOS and web.

02

Place identity files

Add google-services.json, GoogleService-Info.plist, APNs .p8 and the VAPID key.

03

Deploy the sender

Add the service account to the edge function and send through FCM HTTP v1 with the same event kinds.

Order matters: the topic, payload and routing contract already exist. A5 should reuse them; it should not invent a second notification model.

Rollout sequence
01
ConfigureFirebase project and the three app registrations.
02
Install identityPlace the Android, iOS and web credential files.
03
SendDeploy the FCM HTTP v1 edge function and token refresh.
04
VerifyTest killed-app delivery on Android and iOS before claiming it.
Post-rollout verification
CheckPass condition
Token registrationToken stored, refreshed, and removed on sign-out
ForegroundOne alert only; in-app banner remains primary
BackgroundLocal alert follows the same category and quiet-hours gates
Killed appPush received and routed to the correct surface
Client changes

Small: token registration and foreground handler.

Server changes

One sender path in an edge function.

Release claim

Update only after device verification.

PalTuro / dynamic UX change recordVisual evidence
Visual evidence 05 / 05

Privacy, presence and read receipts.

The status layer, as a peer sees it.
Masked at the server.

Presence state machine
AllowedTrack; heartbeat every 60s; show Online or last active.
OffNo track, no heartbeat, no status returned.
Not loadedControls disabled; no optimistic track.
Leave / pauseRemove channel; stop heartbeat.
ErrorTeardown once; retry without re-entrancy.
Receipt rules
  • Seen only under the last own message.
  • Only when the peer allows receipts.
  • Only when the server timestamp covers it.
  • Broadcast is a hint; server reload is the source.
  • Backgrounded broadcasts pause; 60s refresh reconciles.

Consistency: the privacy page, the list and the room all read the same server-masked contract. Turning presence off removes the status everywhere, not just where the toggle was rendered.

Visibility by setting
SettingListRoomReceipts
All onOnline / ActiveOnlineSeen
Presence offMessage timeNo statusSeen if allowed
Typing off—No dotsSeen if allowed
Receipts off—No SeenHidden

Peer view

The list and room never show a status the server did not return for that viewer.

Local view

The owner always sees their own switch state, even when the peer sees nothing.

One contract, three surfaces

The privacy page writes the flags, the conversation RPC masks them per viewer, and the list and room render only what the RPC returned. There is no local “pretend offline” path.

Release statement

Notifications work in-app and through a background process on Android. Activity, badges, banners, local alerts and server reconciliation are verified. Killed-app delivery and guaranteed iOS background delivery are not claimed.

D-02 remains deferred until a store listing exists. A5 remains blocked until Firebase, APNs, VAPID and a service account are supplied.

The product is quieter, more legible, and more truthful about what it knows.

Acceptance is based on three independent audits per phase, live database probes, the final suite, both builds, and the captures in this record.
